svg.text: Hygiene care: the direction of work is the safety rule
Bed bath — the order
1 Face and eyes — water only, no soap
2 Neck, arms, hands, chest, abdomen
3 Legs and feet
4 Back, then pressure area check
5 Perineum LAST — the dirtiest area
Eye care — inner to outer, every time
Swab from the INNER canthus (near the nose)
outward towards the ear.
A FRESH swab for each stroke, and never
the same swab for both eyes.
Wiping outward to inward pushes debris into
the tear duct. One swab for both eyes moves
infection from one eye to the other.
Perineal care direction
FRONT to BACK. Always.
The urethra is clean, the anus is not, and
the female urethra is short.
Wiping backwards to forwards is a leading
cause of urinary tract infection.
Mouth care in the unconscious patient
Turn the head to the SIDE before you start.
Use minimal fluid. Have suction ready.
The risk is aspiration, not a dirty mouth.
Dentures out and cleaned separately, stored
labelled in water. Never wrapped in a tissue.
The recurring pattern in every hygiene procedure
Work from CLEAN towards DIRTY, and never bring a used surface back over a clean one.
Bed bath: face first, perineum last. Eye: inner to outer. Perineum: front to back. Wound: centre outwards.
If an option reverses the direction, it is wrong — whatever else it says about technique.
Also standard: explain and gain consent, ensure privacy, check water temperature, keep the patient covered.
